questions.q: Which opening sounds right for a letter to your cousin: 'I am writing to apprise you of my results' or 'You won't believe it — I passed with 90%!'?
questions.a: The second — informal letters are marked on sounding human. A wrong answer shows the student treats 'letter' as one register — it's relationship-indexed.

questions.q: What is missing: letter with 'Dear Rahul', a body, 'Yours lovingly, Amit'.
questions.a: The address and date — the skeleton still applies even when the register is casual. A wrong answer 'nothing' shows the student thinks informal means structure-free.

questions.q: Which sign-off fits a letter to your grandmother: Yours faithfully / Yours lovingly / Yours sincerely?
questions.a: 'Yours lovingly' — family takes the affectionate pair. A wrong answer 'faithfully' reveals one-size-fits-all sign-off habits.

questions.q: An informal letter to a friend or relative has a light skeleton: your address and date on top, a warm greeting ('Dear Priya'), a chatty body sharing news and asking ______, and a loving sign-off ('Yours lovingly').

Fill in the blank: An informal letter to a friend or relative has a light skeleton: your address and date on top, a warm greeting ('Dear Priya'), a chatty body sharing news and asking ______, and a loving sign-off ('Yours lovingly').
Fill in the blank: Read two openings aloud: 'I am ______ to inform you that I secured first position' vs 'Didi, guess what — I came first!' Same news; the second sounds like a person.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student writes a complete informal letter with correct skeleton and warm register — contractions allowed, questions to the reader included — and can spot a letter that sounds like a formal report.
